newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly, off day high.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly, off day high.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index shed early heavy gains but closed slightly up on Thursday on overseas buying triggered in part by widespread rumours that Beijing would soon outline market-boosting measures, brokers said.
The B index added 1.29 points, or 1.16 percent, to 112.64 after hitting an intraday high of 122.15, with turnover rising to HK$244.35 million from HK$121.09 million on Wednesday.
The A share market ended a bull-run with a plunge due in part to talk that Beijing planned to crack down on recent excessive speculation, brokers said.
The rumours triggered heavy profit-taking following the A market's advances for nine straight sessions, they said.

The A index dived 30.33 points, or 6.58 percent, to 430.50 on turnover of 18.31 billion yuan, compared with 18.82 billion yuan the previous session. The composite index fell 27.12 points, or 6.32 percent, to 402.25.
"The B market was supported by increasing demand from foreign investors but some investors began to cash in on its recent surges," a local broker said.

"Barring major negative news, the index should continue to go up after a short-term correction," the brokers said. "B shares need to consolidate for some sessions because they have gained sharply since last Friday," one analyst said.
"Higher-priced issues, which performed less strongly than third-liners, should become a focus for buying in later sessions," he added.
On the B share market, Weifu was the star, surging HK$0.63, or 15.95 percent, to HK$4.58 on volume of 948,800 shares.

Guangdong Expressway followed suit, rising HK$0.55, or 10.48 percent, to HK$5.80 on trade of 162,900 shares. Changan, the most active counter, put on HK$0.22 to HK$2.50 after 11.39 million shares changed hands.

Donghai added HK$0.08 to HK$2.43, with 9.27 million shares traded. China Bicycle fell HK$0.25, or 9.26 percent, to HK$2.45 on profit-taking, in trading volume of 1.34 million shares, brokers said. Zhonghao fell HK$0.30, or 9.23 percent, to HK$2.95, the second worst performer.
On the A share market, aluminum processor Jiaozuo Wanfang was the biggest loser, plummeting 2.33 yuan, or 14.03 percent, to 14.28 yuan due to profit-taking, brokers said.
Motorcycle maker Hainan Sundiro slumped 3.55 yuan, or 13.98 percent, to 21.85.
